summary:
Project: Build a Construction Simulator for Junior Astronauts

What is the project about?
Our project develops a simulation of a space mission that begins on our natural satellite (the Moon) at a lunar base and heads toward the Red Planet (Mars).

How does it address the challenge?

Our project is a video game that simulates missions involving real-world decisions, from organizing the spacecraft at a lunar outpost to embarking on a journey to the Red Planet. It covers the following aspects: life support (transporting necessary water and oxygen and controlling the spacecraft’s temperature and pressure), solar activity and radiation risk (heliophysical monitoring, hydrogen shielding),  energy management (deployable photovoltaic panels and lithium-ion battery storage), and food production (hydroponic/aeroponic cultivation in microgravity and providing fresh antioxidants to prevent oxidative stress from radiation).

    Why is it important?

The video game is important because it promotes in-depth learning about the reality and significance of what it means to be an astronaut and the duties one must perform, as well as making the right decisions to ensure the mission’s success—all tailored for children ages 7 to 12.

details:
The video game is a simulation of a space mission in which the player controls a character—an astronaut—who must carry out (Pre-flight Operations).

The benefits of this video game include a simulation of making the right decisions—loading necessary supplies such as water and oxygen, controlling the atmosphere inside the spacecraft (temperature and pressure), constantly monitoring the spacecraft’s hull, managing energy, and growing food. All of this is focused on teaching players about the work of an astronaut and the precision required when carrying out pre-flight operations.

Our project primarily aims to engage children ages 7 to 12 by fostering learning and sparking their interest in space.

The tools used were the Godot game development engine and the GDscript programming language.

The project was inspired by the video game *Among Us*. Its creative approach focuses on teaching real-world events that occur throughout an astronaut’s journey, including the precise preparations required for a successful mission.

The development team incorporated real-world data into the game’s design.
